entries.text: All listed cropsClubroot (Finger and Toe)Swollen rootsrecogniseSwollen, distorted roots accompany stunting, purple leaves and wilting in sun. Plants may temporarily revive when cooler.actRemove affected roots; do not home-compost them. There is no cure. Moving brassicas for only a few seasons may be insufficient: soil can remain infected for up to 20 years.preventUse clean transplants, improve drainage and consider resistant varieties. Test pH before liming; long rotations do not guarantee clearance.

All listed cropsCabbage CaterpillarsLarge holes in leavesrecogniseLarge holes in foliage and caterpillars inside hearts indicate cabbage whites, cabbage moths or related species. Check during the warmer months.actInspect regularly and hand-remove eggs and caterpillars. Remove badly infested leaves.preventFit fine mesh before butterflies lay eggs. Keep it clear of leaves and secure the edges.

Kohl RabiWoody Kohl RabirecogniseThe swollen stem becomes hard and fibrous after drought, crowding, slow growth or late harvest.actThere is no cure once woody. Use only parts that remain tender.preventGrow steadily in fertile, moisture-retentive soil. Space correctly, water in dry spells and harvest young unless using a variety bred for large tender stems.

All listed cropsPigeonsrecogniseSoft leaf tissue is stripped away, often leaving stalks and veins. Winter and early spring damage can be severe.actCover vulnerable crops promptly; stripped leaves will not repair themselves.preventKeep taut netting well clear of foliage and secure the edges. Check frequently for trapped wildlife.

All listed cropsFlea BeetleSmall holes in leavesrecogniseTiny jumping beetles pepper young leaves with small round holes. Seedlings are most vulnerable in warm spring weather.actWater damaged seedlings in dry weather so they can outgrow injury.preventProtect susceptible young plants with insect-proof mesh. Raise strong transplants where direct sowings repeatedly fail.

All listed cropsSlugs and SnailsrecogniseIrregular feeding holes and seedling losses are worst in damp weather. Look among loose leaves and open sprouts for hidden slugs.actInspect after dark or in damp conditions and hand-remove slugs around vulnerable plants.preventRaise sturdy transplants. Remove old yellow leaves and damp debris nearby; retain wildlife habitat elsewhere for predators.

All listed cropsCabbage Root FlyTunnelled rootsrecogniseRoot-tunnelling maggots cause wilting, blue-tinged leaves and checked growth. Young plants may die; older plants may fail to form good heads.actRemove badly affected young plants. Older plants sometimes recover if earthed up and kept growing; there is little to do once grubs are inside.preventFit close collars at planting or use fine insect-proof mesh. Rotate crops and remove infected roots.

All listed cropsMealy AphidInsects on leavesrecogniseWaxy grey aphid colonies gather under leaves and on tips, often from June. Leaves curl and yellow; heavy colonies can leave sooty mould.actCheck new growth; squash small damaging colonies by hand while leaving natural predators to help.preventRemove old brassica stalks after cropping and encourage aphid predators.

Brussels SproutsBlown Brussels SproutsrecogniseSprouts become open and leafy rather than tight buttons. Loose soil, drought, crowding and other growth checks contribute.actPick small tender blown sprouts for prompt use; remove larger spoiled ones.preventFirm plants well, give adequate space and water in dry weather. An F1 variety may produce firmer sprouts.

CauliflowerButton CauliflowersrecogniseVery small heads form early and soon run to seed after checks to growth. Pests, poor soil, crowding, drought or nutrient shortages may contribute.actEstablished button heads will not become normal full-sized curds.preventUse rich firm soil, proper spacing and hardened-off plants. Water consistently and prevent early pest damage. Investigate suspected deficiencies before treatment.

All listed cropsCabbage WhiteflyTiny white insects beneath leavesrecogniseTiny white flies lift from leaf undersides when disturbed. Honeydew may support sooty mould; established plants often tolerate them.actUsually tolerate them on outer leaves: damage to edible parts is often slight. Leaf crops such as kale need closer inspection.preventEncourage natural enemies. Glasshouse-whitefly biological controls are not suitable for cabbage whitefly.

CabbageHeartless CabbagesrecogniseDrought, poor fertility, shade, crowding or root damage can prevent firm heads. Check establishment and variety.actCheck moisture and feeding; use balanced nutrition rather than adding straight nitrogen.preventChoose a suitable sunny site, prepare fertile firm ground and plant securely.

CauliflowerWhiptailNarrow leavesrecogniseThin, strap-like cauliflower leaves and very small or absent heads suggest molybdenum deficiency, often associated with acid soil.actConfirm the cause and test soil pH; seek advice on an organic-compatible correction if needed.preventTest pH and correct excessive acidity before the next cauliflower crop.

CauliflowerBoron DeficiencyBrown curdsrecogniseCauliflower leaves distort; curds may be small, brown-spotted or bitter. These signs alone do not confirm boron shortage.actConfirm the deficiency and check pH and moisture. Seek an organic-compatible correction; damaged curds will not repair themselves.preventImprove soil with compost and keep growth steady. Excess boron is toxic: never dose by guesswork.

All listed cropsDiamond-back MothSkin-covered holesrecogniseSmall green caterpillars feed underneath leaves, leaving thin windows of upper skin. Disturbed larvae may drop on a silken thread.actInspect undersides and remove caterpillars on small crops.preventCheck through summer, especially where previous attacks have occurred; use well-secured insect-proof mesh.

All listed cropsDowny MildewrecogniseYellow areas above leaves correspond to white down underneath. Crowded young plants in damp conditions can be badly checked.actRemove affected leaves and severely diseased plants.preventUse clean seed compost, avoid crowding and prolonged wet leaves, and use a fresh seedbed after previous trouble.

All listed cropsWire StemShrunken stemsrecogniseSeedling stem bases blacken and narrow. Plants die or survive with slow growth and brittle stems.actBadly affected seedlings are not worth planting out.preventAvoid cold, wet seed compost and crowding. Use clean trays and fresh compost.

All listed cropsCutwormSevered stemsrecogniseGrey or brown caterpillars hide just below the surface and sever young stems at ground level, often in June and July.actHoe around affected plants and collect caterpillars exposed near damaged stems.preventWhere repeated losses occur, consider an appropriate nematode product, following its temperature and moisture instructions.

CabbageSplit HeartsrecogniseHearts split when rapid growth follows a check, particularly rain after drought. Freezing and thawing can also damage winter heads.actHarvest mature split heads promptly; do not expect the split to heal.preventKeep moisture steady and avoid leaving mature heads standing too long, especially before severe cold.

All listed cropsMagnesium DeficiencyMottling between veinsrecogniseOlder leaves develop yellowing between veins, sometimes followed by reddish or brown areas.actConfirm the problem and check watering, pH and feeding. Seek advice on a suitable organic-compatible magnesium amendment if needed.preventImprove light soil with compost. Avoid excessive potassium feeding, which can reduce magnesium uptake.

All listed cropsFrostCold-damaged leavesrecogniseSevere cold damages exposed heads and leaves, especially where plants are loose. Winter cabbages and savoys tolerate some frost.actAllow healthy growing points to recover. Remove rotting leaves and gently re-firm lifted roots.preventPlant securely and earth up where needed. Harvest sound mature heads before severe weather when appropriate.

All listed cropsWhite Blister (White Rust)recogniseRaised white blisters, mainly beneath leaves, may also affect stems or flowers and distort growth.actRemove affected leaves and reduce crowding.preventAvoid repeating brassicas on the affected ground the following season.

All listed cropsBlack RotrecogniseYellow V-shaped patches spread inward from leaf edges; veins darken and growth is checked. Warm, wet weather favours spread.actRemove and destroy diseased plants. There is no useful cure in the source.preventUse healthy seed and transplants, clear infected debris, rotate and avoid handling wet plants.

All listed cropsChafer GrubsRoots eatenrecogniseWilting plants may have damaged roots and fat, curved grubs in the soil. Recently cultivated grassland is more exposed.actIdentify the grubs before acting; similar soil larvae are not always harmful.preventRemove confirmed damaging grubs found during cultivation. Use nematodes only if labelled for the identified pest and suitable soil conditions.

All listed cropsManganese DeficiencyrecogniseYellowing between veins with curled or scorched edges can resemble other nutrient problems; one leaf is not enough for a firm diagnosis.actCheck soil conditions and confirm the cause. Seek advice on an organic-compatible correction if required.preventMaintain good soil condition and avoid unnecessary liming.

All listed cropsLeaf Spot (Ring Spot)recogniseRinged leaf spots can yellow foliage and cause leaf fall; wet weather favours spread.actRemove badly affected leaves and improve airflow.preventRotate brassicas; avoid the affected site next season.

All listed cropsSwede MidgeBlind plantsrecogniseDistorted stalks near the growing point and blind growth may indicate swede midge. Look for tiny pale larvae and confirm the cause.actRemove badly affected plants. Seek confirmation before attributing unexplained blind growth to this uncommon pest.preventCheck young plants regularly and confirm unexplained growing-point damage.

All listed cropsCabbage Stem Flea BeetleTunnelled stemsrecogniseWilting plants may have cream-coloured grubs inside stems. Attacks occur mainly from August to October.actRemove badly infested plants after checking inside stems to confirm the cause.preventRotate away from affected ground rather than repeating brassicas there next season.

All listed cropsGall WeevilSwollen rootsrecogniseLocal swellings near ground level may cause only slight growth checks. This is usually less serious than club root.actUsually no treatment is worthwhile. Confirm the cause if roots are extensively distorted or plants wilt.preventMonitor affected plants; severe damage needs a fresh diagnosis.

All listed cropsMealy AphidInsects on leavesrecogniseWaxy grey aphid colonies gather under leaves and on tips, often from June. Leaves curl and yellow; heavy colonies can leave sooty mould.actCheck new growth; squash small damaging colonies by hand while leaving natural predators to help.preventRemove old brassica stalks after cropping and encourage aphid predators.

Brussels SproutsBlown Brussels SproutsrecogniseSprouts become open and leafy rather than tight buttons. Loose soil, drought, crowding and other growth checks contribute.actPick small tender blown sprouts for prompt use; remove larger spoiled ones.preventFirm plants well, give adequate space and water in dry weather. An F1 variety may produce firmer sprouts.

CauliflowerButton CauliflowersrecogniseVery small heads form early and soon run to seed after checks to growth. Pests, poor soil, crowding, drought or nutrient shortages may contribute.actEstablished button heads will not become normal full-sized curds.preventUse rich firm soil, proper spacing and hardened-off plants. Water consistently and prevent early pest damage. Investigate suspected deficiencies before treatment.

All listed cropsCabbage WhiteflyTiny white insects beneath leavesrecogniseTiny white flies lift from leaf undersides when disturbed. Honeydew may support sooty mould; established plants often tolerate them.actUsually tolerate them on outer leaves: damage to edible parts is often slight. Leaf crops such as kale need closer inspection.preventEncourage natural enemies. Glasshouse-whitefly biological controls are not suitable for cabbage whitefly.

CabbageHeartless CabbagesrecogniseDrought, poor fertility, shade, crowding or root damage can prevent firm heads. Check establishment and variety.actCheck moisture and feeding; use balanced nutrition rather than adding straight nitrogen.preventChoose a suitable sunny site, prepare fertile firm ground and plant securely.

CauliflowerWhiptailNarrow leavesrecogniseThin, strap-like cauliflower leaves and very small or absent heads suggest molybdenum deficiency, often associated with acid soil.actConfirm the cause and test soil pH; seek advice on an organic-compatible correction if needed.preventTest pH and correct excessive acidity before the next cauliflower crop.

CauliflowerBoron DeficiencyBrown curdsrecogniseCauliflower leaves distort; curds may be small, brown-spotted or bitter. These signs alone do not confirm boron shortage.actConfirm the deficiency and check pH and moisture. Seek an organic-compatible correction; damaged curds will not repair themselves.preventImprove soil with compost and keep growth steady. Excess boron is toxic: never dose by guesswork.

All listed cropsDowny MildewrecogniseYellow areas above leaves correspond to white down underneath. Crowded young plants in damp conditions can be badly checked.actRemove affected leaves and severely diseased plants.preventUse clean seed compost, avoid crowding and prolonged wet leaves, and use a fresh seedbed after previous trouble.

All listed cropsDiamond-back MothSkin-covered holesrecogniseSmall green caterpillars feed underneath leaves, leaving thin windows of upper skin. Disturbed larvae may drop on a silken thread.actInspect undersides and remove caterpillars on small crops.preventCheck through summer, especially where previous attacks have occurred; use well-secured insect-proof mesh.

All listed cropsWire StemShrunken stemsrecogniseSeedling stem bases blacken and narrow. Plants die or survive with slow growth and brittle stems.actBadly affected seedlings are not worth planting out.preventAvoid cold, wet seed compost and crowding. Use clean trays and fresh compost.

All listed cropsCutwormSevered stemsrecogniseGrey or brown caterpillars hide just below the surface and sever young stems at ground level, often in June and July.actHoe around affected plants and collect caterpillars exposed near damaged stems.preventWhere repeated losses occur, consider an appropriate nematode product, following its temperature and moisture instructions.

CabbageSplit HeartsrecogniseHearts split when rapid growth follows a check, particularly rain after drought. Freezing and thawing can also damage winter heads.actHarvest mature split heads promptly; do not expect the split to heal.preventKeep moisture steady and avoid leaving mature heads standing too long, especially before severe cold.

All listed cropsMagnesium DeficiencyMottling between veinsrecogniseOlder leaves develop yellowing between veins, sometimes followed by reddish or brown areas.actConfirm the problem and check watering, pH and feeding. Seek advice on a suitable organic-compatible magnesium amendment if needed.preventImprove light soil with compost. Avoid excessive potassium feeding, which can reduce magnesium uptake.

All listed cropsFrostCold-damaged leavesrecogniseSevere cold damages exposed heads and leaves, especially where plants are loose. Winter cabbages and savoys tolerate some frost.actAllow healthy growing points to recover. Remove rotting leaves and gently re-firm lifted roots.preventPlant securely and earth up where needed. Harvest sound mature heads before severe weather when appropriate.

All listed cropsWhite Blister (White Rust)recogniseRaised white blisters, mainly beneath leaves, may also affect stems or flowers and distort growth.actRemove affected leaves and reduce crowding.preventAvoid repeating brassicas on the affected ground the following season.

All listed cropsBlack RotrecogniseYellow V-shaped patches spread inward from leaf edges; veins darken and growth is checked. Warm, wet weather favours spread.actRemove and destroy diseased plants. There is no useful cure in the source.preventUse healthy seed and transplants, clear infected debris, rotate and avoid handling wet plants.

All listed cropsChafer GrubsRoots eatenrecogniseWilting plants may have damaged roots and fat, curved grubs in the soil. Recently cultivated grassland is more exposed.actIdentify the grubs before acting; similar soil larvae are not always harmful.preventRemove confirmed damaging grubs found during cultivation. Use nematodes only if labelled for the identified pest and suitable soil conditions.

All listed cropsManganese DeficiencyrecogniseYellowing between veins with curled or scorched edges can resemble other nutrient problems; one leaf is not enough for a firm diagnosis.actCheck soil conditions and confirm the cause. Seek advice on an organic-compatible correction if required.preventMaintain good soil condition and avoid unnecessary liming.

All listed cropsLeaf Spot (Ring Spot)recogniseRinged leaf spots can yellow foliage and cause leaf fall; wet weather favours spread.actRemove badly affected leaves and improve airflow.preventRotate brassicas; avoid the affected site next season.

All listed cropsSwede MidgeBlind plantsrecogniseDistorted stalks near the growing point and blind growth may indicate swede midge. Look for tiny pale larvae and confirm the cause.actRemove badly affected plants. Seek confirmation before attributing unexplained blind growth to this uncommon pest.preventCheck young plants regularly and confirm unexplained growing-point damage.

All listed cropsCabbage Stem Flea BeetleTunnelled stemsrecogniseWilting plants may have cream-coloured grubs inside stems. Attacks occur mainly from August to October.actRemove badly infested plants after checking inside stems to confirm the cause.preventRotate away from affected ground rather than repeating brassicas there next season.

All listed cropsGall WeevilSwollen rootsrecogniseLocal swellings near ground level may cause only slight growth checks. This is usually less serious than club root.actUsually no treatment is worthwhile. Confirm the cause if roots are extensively distorted or plants wilt.preventMonitor affected plants; severe damage needs a fresh diagnosis.
